description: Insiyab for Avalonia: the glass, RTL-first design system as Avalonia themes.
releaseNotes:
0.4.0

Android
- The library runs on Android in a single view as it does in a window; the Windows-only parts (window material, title bar, tray icon, taskbar badge) stay quiet on other systems.
- Safe areas: `ins:SafeArea.Edges` pads by the system bars and cutouts; overlays keep clear of the bars and the on-screen keyboard; an edge-to-edge view gives the status bar a band of its own.
- Back (Android's button or gesture, a mouse's back button) closes the newest library overlay, then goes back a page.
- Touch: a finger is told from a mouse (no hover after a tap, no tap while scrolling, a long press for menus, tips and words); small controls reach 44px under a finger (`ins:TouchTarget.Size` for more); a press's look is held a moment after release; scrollbars show only while scrolling.
- Follows Android's Remove animations. `InsiyabTheme.Effects = EffectsLevel.Light` lightens the costliest drawing (no blur behind a dialog, lighter soft shadows) and turns on by itself on a device low on memory or with less than 3.5 GB.

New
- `BottomNav` and `BottomNavItem`: a phone's bottom tab bar whose brand pill flies to the chosen page, with badges and dots; `IsRail` stands it at the start side in a short window.
- `PageStack`: pages that slide over one another and go back by Back, a swipe or a call.
- Bottom sheet: a `drawer bottom` dialog in a single view (or with `sheet`) has a handle, a pull to close and room for the gesture bar.
- Pull to refresh: `RefreshContainer` wears the brand spinner on a glass disc, starts only from the top of the list and follows the finger with resistance.
- The `fab` look (`fab`, `fab sm`, `fab extended`): a round brand button floating at the end of the page's foot, clear of the bars and the keyboard.
- `Meter` and `MeterPart`: a whole in parts, as a phone's storage bar.
- `ins:Dot.IsShown`: the new-item dot on any control. `ins:Tone.Class`: a tone class from data.
- `PictureWindow`: a small window kept over the others for a picture watched beside other work. `PlayPauseIcon`, `Marquee`.
- `SlidePages`: menu pages that slide in and out. `PopCard.GrowsFromCorner`: a menu that grows from its corner nearest the trigger.
- `PickerField`: a field that opens a list to pick from.
- `BrushFade`: the library's brush transition, meeting in premultiplied colour. `MarkGlide`: the selection flight for a mark an app draws itself. `DirectionFlip`: a language and direction change inside the page turn.
- Month calendar on a phone: `NarrowLayout`, `DetailsPresentation` (details in a bottom sheet), `ShowHeader`, a sideways swipe between periods, two events a day, and event titles that break between whole words.
- `Segmented` scrolls sideways and keeps its choice in view; the `chips` look is a filter chip row; `SegmentedItem.IsLink` leads out of the row.
- `CommandPalette` opens full screen on a phone. `ProgressRing.Text` and `Caption`. `DateBadge.Icon`. `DialogFoot` stands its actions one under the other on a phone when a label would be cut. Steps show a window around the current one when the row is narrow. The notifications panel can hold a line under its head.

Changed
- A still window (effects off) keeps short colour and opacity fades (150 ms at most) while nothing moves.
- Every visible item of a menu rises in as it opens, not only the first five; separators stay still.
- The top bar folds step by step to the room it has; photos in lists and the sidebar line up with icons.
- A table's read-only cells use a lighter template; an entrance never leaves content hidden.

The full list of 0.3.0 changes is on the 0.3.0 release.
